title: SupplyLane — from incomplete to ready for review
audience: Procurement coordinators, with requesters as the secondary customer
decision: Agree one request type to test with fictional sample data
premise: Incomplete purchase requests create repeated clarification before review; a guided intake could make the handoff clearer.
status: Fictional planning example. All product behavior is proposed; no implementation, customer result or approval is claimed.

beats.headline: Before review, the missing details
beats.speech: Before a purchase request can be reviewed, someone has to chase the missing details. This fictional SupplyLane concept shows another way the handoff could work.
beats.visual: A clearly labeled concept screen shows request REQ-104 for office chairs, with delivery date absent and a clarification message beside it.
beats.proof: Establishes the invented workflow problem, not its frequency or cost.
beats.source: Fictional SupplyLane scenario in examples/pitch-demo-brief.md; author assumptions, not observed product behavior.
beats.delivery: Warm recognition; leave a short pause after missing details.
beats.data_provenance: Invented request REQ-104 and sample purchasing data; no real organization, customer or endorsement.

beats.headline: Complete information. Decision still pending.
beats.speech: Here is the proposed outcome: one complete request, ready for a person to review. It has not been approved, and no order has been placed.
beats.visual: Glimpse REQ-104 in a proposed coordinator queue. Complete information and Pending review appear as separate labels.
beats.proof: Shows the intended output shape; does not prove software execution or automatic purchasing.
beats.source: Fictional SupplyLane scenario in examples/pitch-demo-brief.md; author assumptions, not observed product behavior.
beats.delivery: Assured but restrained; hold on Pending review.
beats.data_provenance: Invented request REQ-104 and sample purchasing data; no real organization, customer or endorsement.

beats.headline: Back to the requester
beats.speech: Now back to the requester. Before sending, the form points out what is missing and explains what to add.
beats.visual: Explicit rewind label. Show the earlier REQ-104 form with the required delivery-date field highlighted.
beats.proof: Makes the time jump visible and introduces the proposed presubmission correction.
beats.source: Fictional SupplyLane scenario in examples/pitch-demo-brief.md; author assumptions, not observed product behavior.
beats.delivery: Matter-of-fact; align the field reveal with what is missing.
beats.data_provenance: Invented request REQ-104 and sample purchasing data; no real organization, customer or endorsement.

beats.headline: Fix it while the context is fresh
beats.speech: In this design, adding the delivery date clears that warning. The requester can check the complete summary before sending it.
beats.visual: Planned transition: enter a fictional delivery date; clear only that warning; show request summary and Submit for review button.
beats.proof: Illustrates a required-field correction, not a complete validation engine or proof that the request is suitable.
beats.source: Fictional SupplyLane scenario in examples/pitch-demo-brief.md; author assumptions, not observed product behavior.
beats.delivery: Conversational; pause while the viewer reads the corrected field.
beats.data_provenance: Invented request REQ-104 and sample purchasing data; no real organization, customer or endorsement.

beats.headline: The same request, ready to inspect
beats.speech: After submission, the coordinator would see that same request with the information together. The review decision stays with the coordinator.
beats.visual: Switch role label to Procurement coordinator. REQ-104 remains Pending review and retains the same items and delivery date.
beats.proof: Preserves request continuity and human authority; no approval is staged.
beats.source: Fictional SupplyLane scenario in examples/pitch-demo-brief.md; author assumptions, not observed product behavior.
beats.delivery: Calm confidence; emphasize same request, not the product name.
beats.data_provenance: Invented request REQ-104 and sample purchasing data; no real organization, customer or endorsement.

beats.headline: The requester knows where it stands
beats.speech: The requester would see that it is waiting for review, too. A complete submission does not have to leave them guessing what happened next.
beats.visual: Return to requester view. Show REQ-104, Submitted receipt and Pending review. No invented approval-time estimate.
beats.proof: Shows the secondary customer benefit in the proposed design without a delivery-time promise.
beats.source: Fictional SupplyLane scenario in examples/pitch-demo-brief.md; author assumptions, not observed product behavior.
beats.delivery: Reassuring, without implying an approval outcome.
beats.data_provenance: Invented request REQ-104 and sample purchasing data; no real organization, customer or endorsement.

beats.headline: Try one request type
beats.speech: The proposed change is simple: catch missing details before the handoff, and make the next step visible to both people. Let us choose one request type to test with sample data.
beats.visual: Return to the two role views, then display the proposed next step as plain text. No booking link or send action.
beats.proof: Connects the proposed mechanism to the initial problem and requests a scoped next step, not a purchase.
beats.source: Fictional SupplyLane scenario in examples/pitch-demo-brief.md; author assumptions, not observed product behavior.
beats.delivery: Clear invitation; leave a visual hold after the final line.
beats.data_provenance: Invented request REQ-104 and sample purchasing data; no real organization, customer or endorsement.
